result.label: Plastic modeling
result.summary: Scale plastic modeling is the hobby of assembling and painting miniature replicas of aircraft, vehicles, ships and figures from kits.

children.label: Kits
children.summary: A plastic kit is a set of injection-molded parts on runners (sprues) that you cut, clean, glue and paint into a miniature replica.

children.label: Tools
children.summary: A small kit of cutters, knives, files and glue covers nearly every beginner build.

children.label: Paints & Finishing
children.summary: Painting and finishing give a model color, depth and a protective surface.

children.label: Techniques
children.summary: Core building and painting methods learned step by step.

children.label: Scales & Subjects
children.summary: Scale is the size ratio of the model to the real thing; subject is what it depicts.

children.label: History
children.summary: The hobby grew from wooden and metal models into mass-produced plastic kits after WWII.

children.label: Community
children.summary: Clubs, forums and shows are where beginners learn fastest.

children.label: Workspace & Safety
children.summary: Good lighting, ventilation and organization make building safe and enjoyable.

children.label: Injection-molded kits
children.summary: Styrene parts are molded on runners; the standard format for cars, planes, ships and armor.

children.label: Snap-fit kits
children.summary: Parts click together with pegs and sockets; often marketed as easy or starter kits with color-molded plastic.

children.label: Resin and 3D-printed kits
children.summary: Small-batch casts or prints used for rare subjects and upgrades; they need washing, curing and different glue.

children.label: Gunpla
children.summary: Plastic kits of Gundam mecha, known for color-separated parts and articulated joints.

children.label: Beginner-friendly brands
children.summary: Tamiya, Revell, Airfix and Bandai are widely recommended for good fit and clear instructions.

children.label: Reading the instructions
children.summary: Instruction sheets show part numbers, paint call-outs and assembly order; test-fit before gluing.

branchLinks.why: Injection-molded styrene kits are assembled with solvent cement.
Resin does not melt with plastic cement, so CA glue is used.
Gunpla is the product of that history.
Airfix was a pioneer of the postwar boom.
